text:
Investigate this suspected problem.

Suspect S1: Helper function defined inside another function but used before definition
Category: correctness
Location: src/werkzeug/utils.py lines 178-178 (new version)
Suspected problem: The helper function _wants_charset is called at line 178 inside get_content_type, but it is defined further down at line 184. In Python, inner functions are evaluated at runtime when the execution reaches the def statement, so calling _wants_charset before it is defined will raise a NameError.
What would confirm or refute it: Check the relative order of the 'if _wants_charset(mimetype):' call and the 'def _wants_charset(mimetype):' definition within get_content_type.

evidence.note: _wants_charset is defined at the module level outside get_content_type
get_content_type calls _wants_charset after it has been defined above it in the module

arguments.claim: The helper function _wants_charset is defined at the module level rather than inside get_content_type, so it is already defined when called and will not raise a NameError.
arguments.explanation: Although the suspect claimed that _wants_charset was defined inside get_content_type after its call, reading the actual code at HEAD shows that _wants_charset is defined at the module level (below get_content_type), meaning it is fully defined and bound before get_content_type is called at runtime. Thus, no NameError occurs.
